payload.feature:
THE PROOFS — branch integration/226-resume-prepared at HEAD 4daaa7d. Two items: the decision-level proofs your predecessor owed, and the six lines and one branch its own new code left uncovered. Nothing else.

ADOPT, DO NOT REWORK. Run the-whole-family-branch-integrat-0a5cdb4f parked at IMPL-OVERSIZED-EXHAUSTED having delivered the production repairs. Its commits stand and its design is settled. Read its return notes before anything else. In summary of what is already true at your head:

  - The execution-site family is ONE structure: `Bundle.sites`, a canonical table owning the inline assessment, the driver pins, hands as a tri-state (unknown / no-hands / hands), the agent record and the driver evidence. `relocate_verify_facts` drains every source before inserting any destination, so `verify -> verify:checks` and `verify:<m> -> verify:checks:<m>` carry the whole value, the overlapping `x` / `checks:x` shapes included.
  - Absence never enables. The engine publishes affirmative markers per dispatch and `resume_gate` requires both as recognised strings; missing, null, non-string or unknown decline with `restrictions-unavailable`, and an absent assessment or accounting stays `unsupported-resume`.
  - Global aliasing is closed by `owner_index`, a structural census of every authoring owner run on the authoring bodies BEFORE the wrapper renames an address and again on the final bodies, with exact source/destination pairs. That closes the raw wrapped-member alias, the wrapper-created `verify:checks` and `verify:dialect-verify` aliases, and the prefix-sweep theft of an unrelated literal phase.
  - Runtime hands, boundary and spawn composition read `Bundle.sites` rather than a serialization projection, so the tri-state survives.
  - Four removal proofs were observed and restored: deleting the authoring census, reintroducing the prefix sweep, inserting destinations without draining, and deleting the dispatch-time mark each made a named test fail.

ITEM 1 — THE DECISION-LEVEL PROOFS. The standing commission asked that each fix be driven to the GATE'S DECISION rather than to the shape of a map, and your predecessor said plainly that this is what it ran out of room for. The four shapes that must each be proved at the decision, live or refused with the right token:

  (a) a single inline Codex seat, wrapped by dialect verification — supported rejoin comes out LIVE;
  (b) a hands-bearing inline Codex panel member, wrapped — this is the shape that went FAIL-OPEN in an earlier attempt and was reverted; it must come out refused with `restrictions-unavailable` when its confinement cannot be affirmed, and live only when the markers are affirmatively correct;
  (c) a no-hands inline Codex panel member, wrapped — this is the mirror that was WRONGLY DECLINED; a supported retry comes out live;
  (d) the unwrapped forms of all three, unchanged from today.

  A test that asserts the contents of `Bundle.sites` does not discharge this. The assertion is on what the provider gate decides and which token it names.

ITEM 2 — YOUR PREDECESSOR'S OWN UNCOVERED CODE. The exact gate refuses at your head. Measured on the host: lines 30,269 of 30,275, branches 5,039 of 5,040, functions 2,890 of 2,890. All of the residue is in `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs` and all of it is new:

    line 1528-1531  assemble        the `_ =>` refusal: "dialect verify currently requires a single or panel verify seat"
    line 1780       owner_index     the `Some(_) => {}` arm
    line 3042       parse_selected_body  the `)?;` continuation
    branch at 1770

  Cover each, or, if one is genuinely unreachable, answer it the way this branch has answered three dead guards before: remove the guard together with the invariant that makes it unreachable, or state the rule once where a test can reach it. Never by deleting a rule the change's accepted delta requires, and never with a `#[cfg(...)]` exclusion or `coverage(off)` — the script refuses those by design.

THE RULES THAT DO NOT MOVE.

  - **The family stays indivisible.** A partial relocation is not partial progress. If you touch the relocation at all, it moves whole or not at all.
  - **Absence still declines.** Do not weaken the marker requirement to make a proof easier to write.
  - **Do not trade safety for the operator's ruling.** The ruling is that a Codex rejoin main performs today stays live. It is not licence to enable a shape whose confinement is unknown. If a case cannot be both live and safe, it stays refused and you say so.
  - **Windows.** `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/process.rs` invokes Command directly, so no shell interprets a shebang. A test that writes a script and uses it as argv[0] is `#[cfg(unix)]` or uses a real executable. The first Windows and macOS signal always arrives from CI after a push, never from a local suite.

PROVE YOUR WORK. Break the line each new test claims, watch it fail, restore, say so. Report the gate's own before and after numbers for all three measures.

NOT YOURS. Passes C and D. Ticking 8.8, 8.10, 9.6 or any 11.x task. Archiving the change. Re-folding the five living specs this reconciliation withdrew. Editing frozen contracts, policy, reference or fixtures. Re-planning what is settled — five design passes have now been spent on this branch and the design is not the problem. Close these two items.

HOW TO MEASURE COVERAGE. Use a writable disk-backed TMPDIR OUTSIDE the repository; an in-repo TMPDIR breaks the ledger tests and the box's global TMPDIR may be read-only from a seat. The boundary tests skip inside the box, which cannot create a bwrap namespace on this host, so in-box equality is unattainable and is not your failure (#286). Report your in-box numbers; the host measurement is the controller's.

IF YOU RUN OUT OF ROOM. Return `oversized`, never `broken`. Item 2 is small and concrete; if you can only do one, do item 1, because it is the one that says the repair is correct.

KNOWN ENVIRONMENT DEFECTS — do not rediscover them. #282: the installed DSH core forwards GIT_CONFIG_COUNT but filters GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0, so prefix any git call, git init in tests included, with `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0`. #281: a DeepSeek seat records no turns and no tokens; a harness defect.

PROVIDER INSTRUCTION. No Claude seat; the Fable allowance is spent. Codex (gpt-6-astra at xhigh) holds triage, clarify, the chief architect, analyze and the review chief. DeepSeek (the stable deepseek-v4-flash alias, never the expiring experimental one) holds implement, the task planner and every design and review position.

REVIEW POSITIONS state findings and evidence. They do not direct a verdict, do not tell a gate where to send the work, and do not claim another office's power.

CONSTRAINTS. fmt, clippy across all targets and features, the crate suites, both bundle compiles and strict OpenSpec validation must all pass. Commit completed work unsigned. Never push, merge, or start another Brokkr run from a seat; the controller owns remote CI, publication, integration and closure.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```
